headline: Comparative genomics links shark epigenomics, telomeric introns and Wnt gene evolution
label: Comparative Functional Genomics Inference
summary: Recent comparisons across shark, eukaryotic, and vertebrate genomes address intron origins, methylation, and gene family dynamics.
synthesis: The common thread is comparative inference of genome architecture and evolutionary history from large sequence sets. A chromosome-scale, haplotype-phased tiger shark genome is combined with methylomic and hydroxymethylomic data, reporting male heterogamety, transposable element expansions, and demographic history. Telotrons, spliceosomal introns composed mostly of telomeric repeats, were identified across 10,310 eukaryotic genome assemblies and linked to intron gain. A vertebrate Wnt study of 38,886 sequences from 1,961 vertebrates quantifies copy-number variation, whole-genome duplication effects, and dN/dS rates. Together these items apply comparative and population-level frameworks to structural and gene-family change over evolutionary time. What is new is the joint treatment of epigenomic profiling, genome-wide intron surveys, and gene repertoire dynamics.
